newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban play down fighting in eastern Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Taleban play down fighting in eastern Afghanistan.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban militia has sent reinforcements to the eastern province of Kunar, a Taleban official said on Thursday, but he played down the significance of fighting in the area.
"During (the Islamic holiday of) Eid the enemy launched an attack." Taleban Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi said.
"Yesterday government forces cleared the opposition and recaptured the area. Some 500 men have been sent as reinforcements," Mutaqi told reporters.
There was no independent confirmation of his comments.
Mutaqi said the opposition had not captured any significant territory.
"The ground that the opposition managed to capture was mostly deserted mountainous areas where there was no Taleban presence." he said.
The Taleban have taken control of about two-thirds of Afghanistan since capturing the Afghan capital Kabul on September 27.
Mutaqi denied speculation that the opposition had advanced close to Kunar's provincial capital, Assadabad.
"They haven't captured any important areas and are not near Assadabad. We have only sent reinforcements to prevent infiltration from Badakshan province." he said.
Badakshan, on Kunar's northern border, is held by troops loyal to the anti-Taleban alliance of ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood and northern General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
Kunar is some 200 km (125 miles) east of Kabul on the border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Mutaqi said fighting had died down on Thursday but that the Taleban intended to carry out the operation.
"The situation was normal today, but we intend to clear the rest of the area where we believe the enemy to be," he said.
The Taleban, who are committed to bringing their strict version of Islamic sharia law to the country, have scored significant victories over the opposition alliance in the past month.
In two offensives they managed to drive the alliance forces back about 70 km (40 miles).
The front line north of Kabul is now about 110 km (70 miles) from the city.
At the same news conference on Thursday, Mutaqi said an amnesty offered by the Taleban earlier in the week was not extended to leaders of the opposition.
"The amnesty is for the people who had no choice but to work with the opposition. The big commanders such as Dostum are not included." he said.
